Which maintenance window is this? We have two: the 01:00–03:00 UTC ops window and the 22:00–24:00 UTC reporting window.
The plan assumed the ops window, 01:00–03:00 UTC. I'll confirm with the database team before the first night.
While you're at it, check that the replica can take the write load.
Checked: in the soak test the replica sustained 2,400 writes a second, above the 1,900 the copy needs.
Decision from today's DB sync: the copy runs in the 22:00–24:00 UTC reporting window, because the vacuum job now owns the ops window. Don't schedule anything at 01:00–03:00.
Understood: 22:00–24:00 UTC, and nothing in the ops window.
Is 500 rows per batch right? It feels small, and eleven nights is a long time to keep an eye on this. Could we go bigger and finish in fewer nights?

At 500 rows the replica's lag stays under two seconds for the whole window. At 2,000 it reached eleven seconds within twenty minutes, and the reporting dashboards read from that replica, so larger batches would show finance stale numbers. I'd keep 500 and accept the eleven nights.
Fine, keep 500. What happens if a night's batch fails halfway through? I don't want duplicated orders in the warehouse.

The job stops at the first failed batch and records the last committed one. The next night resumes from there, and every batch is an upsert keyed on the order id, so no order is copied twice even if a batch is retried.
Who gets paged if it stops? The data-platform rotation is thin this month.

The data-platform on-call. The alert fires when a night ends with the copy stopped rather than on the first failure, so a transient error that the retry absorbs doesn't wake anyone. I checked the rotation: two people cover October.
Add finance to the notification list too, they watch the year-over-year numbers and will ask why a night is missing.
Added: finance-reporting gets the nightly summary each morning, with rows copied, rows remaining, and any failed batch. They don't get the page itself, since they can't act on it.
Good. Any risk to the 16 October end date? The cutover can't move.
Only a failed night, which pushes the end back a day. There are over two weeks of slack before the 3 November cutover, so it would take more than a dozen failed nights to threaten it.
What about the storage on the warehouse side? Last quarter we ran out of space during a much smaller import.

The warehouse has 9.2 TB free and the full history is about 2.1 TB once compressed, so the copy uses under a quarter of the headroom. I also asked the warehouse team to raise the quota alert from 80% to 90% for October so it doesn't fire on the expected growth.
How will we know the copy is complete and correct, beyond the job saying it finished?

After the last night, a check compares row counts and a checksum of order totals per month between the primary and the warehouse. Any month that differs is recopied on its own. The check takes about forty minutes and runs the morning after the final night.
Who signs off on that check before the dashboards move?
The reporting team's lead signs off, since their dashboards are the ones that move. I'll post the check's per-month results on this page so the sign-off has something concrete to point at.
OK. Last thing: do we need a change ticket for this?
Yes, a standard change covering all eleven nights. I filed it this morning with the schedule, the rollback plan, and the paging arrangement, and it's approved for the October change window.
